major_concerns: Validator fidelity may not reflect production behavior (emulator vs real device) — drives primary outcome.
Corpus representativeness: public/synthetic configs may not match real operator intents.
Definition of "harmful misconfiguration" depends on oracle/validator design and may conflate syntactic vs semantic harms.
Repair-iteration cap N could mask slow-converging fixes or divergent repair behavior.
Multi-vendor semantics and proprietary features may be hard to model consistently.
required_design_repairs: Specify concrete validator implementations (e.g., Batfish, Mininet/emulator, vendor-specific models) and their limitations.
Pre-register dataset sources with links and inclusion/exclusion rules; provide public splits and sampling procedure.
Precisely define the oracle "harmful" label (invariants tested, severity threshold) and justify reachability/isolation checks.
Pre-register repair loop details: prompt templates, iteration cap N, stopping rules, retry policy, and random seeds.
Add sensitivity analyses for validator fidelity, dataset sources, and repair-cap choices; log disagreements between validators.

major_concerns: Heavily dependent on labeled data (harm labels) produced by c2026-001 or equivalent — risk of circularity.
Metric definitions are currently high-level and may overfit the constructed workload.
Oracle labels inherit validator-fidelity biases; metric training may learn validator artifacts rather than real operational risk.
Combining heterogeneous metrics risks poor calibration without sufficient sample size.
required_design_repairs: Provide precise, reproducible definitions/formulae for each metric (grounding_coverage, validator_coverage, semantic_impact_score, etc.).
Ensure independence: pre-register held-out vendor splits and do not reuse training tasks from c2026-001 without separation.
Specify modeling pipeline for combining metrics (logistic/regression/ensemble), cross-validation plan, and calibration procedures.
Quantify minimum sample-size needed for stable AUC/CIs and include robustness checks for metric sensitivity to validator errors.

major_concerns: Formal verifiers are underspecified — different tools offer different semantics and performance characteristics.
Vendor-specific semantics (ACLs, vendor CLI quirks) may not be captured by verifier, inflating false positives/negatives.
Verifier timeouts or inconclusive results could bias TP/FP estimates and downstream throughput calculations.
Scaling claims depend on chosen topology/config complexity distributions which are not yet defined.
required_design_repairs: Specify the exact verifier(s) (e.g., Batfish, symbolic model checker) and versions; document supported semantics and known gaps.
Define topology/config complexity bins quantitatively (nodes, ACL rules, number of changed lines) and justify realism.
Prespecify timeout policies, handling of inconclusive results, and how those are counted in TP/FP analysis.
Include fallback or approximate-verification modes and report their effect; preregister acceptable FP/latency thresholds and measurement procedures.

major_concerns: Simulated operator model calibration is underspecified and may not reflect real operator behavior or error distributions.
Strong dependence on literature-derived latency/accuracy estimates — those sources may be sparse or context-specific.
Simulation outcomes risk being mistaken for real HITL performance; ecological validity is limited without empirical operator logs.
Choice of ambiguity labeling for intents may be subjective and affect conclusions.
required_design_repairs: Define the simulated-operator model precisely (response accuracy distribution, latency distribution, decision heuristics) with literature citations and numeric parameters.
Prespecify ambiguity classification rules for intents and how tasks are partitioned into clear vs ambiguous.
Run extensive sensitivity analyses over operator-accuracy and latency parameters; report robustness bounds.
If possible, locate and use any public operator-interaction logs for partial calibration or explicitly state limitations if none exist.
